name: Nadab
overview: Nadab was a male member of the tribe of Levi and the son of Aaron. He is notably remembered for his death as a result of offering unauthorized fire before the LORD. This act is recorded in the book of Numbers and highlights his significant, yet tragic, role in the priestly lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Nadab means 'volunteer' or 'free will offering,' reflecting a sense of willing service. This name is noted in Exodus 6:23 and is a proper name not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Nadab was the son of Aaron and Elisheba, as indicated in Exodus 6:23 and Numbers 26:60. These family ties place him within the priestly family line of the Levites.
scriptureSignificance: Nadab's significance lies in his role as a priestly son who failed to uphold the holiness required by God, evidenced by his death for offering strange fire. This event serves as a solemn reminder of the sanctity of worship and the seriousness of obedience to God's commands within the Levitical priesthood.
